text: Yeah, so that is the last part of it i guess to ask is a ramp does pretty much a strict 45 angle so how would we do a bridge then since a heightfield can smooth its incline with distance but it lifts the ground under it unlike a ramp does
resolution: Answered the bridge-approach question (no code changed): the premise that a heightfield lifts the ground under it is false — heightfield colliders are floating surface skins, not filled volumes; physics.zig explicitly anticipates garages/ramps/overpasses as heightfield floors ON TOP of terrain, the current_y+step gating makes the space under any heightfield traversable, and the parking garage already uses a rotated floating heightfield as its drivable ramp. Bridge approaches therefore = thin floating heightfield strips the road stroke generates, climbing from ground to deck height at a road grade (~10-15 percent, approach run visualized in the tool), open underneath, with a matching rendered slab and lane kinds on its 1m surface cells. The 45-degree catalog ramp stays buildings-only. This closes the last gap: all four road bases (trail/tunnel/subway/bridge incl. getting onto it) compile from one stroke painter out of three surface primitives (painted ground, lifted 3x3 floors, floating heightfield strips) + the terrain hole mask.
